attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own Substack post, not a quotation of someone else.

semantics.note: 'Will tighten' is a firm forecast with no deadline. Reading 'budgets' as enterprise AI budgets fits the tokenmaxxing context. The 'especially when' clause is kept as an amplifier, not a precondition.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: companies broadly cutting, capping or slowing AI spend against plan. Neither side can be finally settled without a deadline; only the early-support rule can resolve it, and that is fair.

evidence.note: Sept 2026 CIO survey (n=1,636): 46.9% over AI budget vs 5.6% below. This weighs against broad tightening so far, but it cannot contradict an open-ended forecast and does not meet the early-support rule.
Only 17.2% of over-budget firms pause or cut AI work; most ask for more money or absorb the overrun. A small minority fits Marcus's view, which is not broad tightening.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The only post-statement data, Futurum's Sept 2026 survey, shows spend running over plan at most firms and few cutting back, so the early-support rule is not met. With an open horizon the forecast cannot be contradicted yet, so it stays unresolved.

attribution.note: An aside in Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The parenthetical states a present fact. The implied baseline (ordinary or chat use) is a fair reading, and the plural 'orders of magnitude' is kept.

contract.note: Reading plural 'orders of magnitude' as about 100x or more is ordinary, as is a chat baseline. The result turns on which kind of agent and which baseline, neither of which Marcus specified.

evidence.note: April 2026 preprint: agentic coding tasks on SWE-bench use about 1000x the tokens of code chat. That is several orders of magnitude, within the period.
Secondary report of Gartner's March 2026 estimate: agentic workflows use 5-30x the tokens of a chatbot query, at most one order of magnitude. Published Aug 2026, before the evaluation date.
Anthropic's own 2025 figures (agents about 4x, multi-agent about 15x chat) predate the target period and are a company disclosure. Context only.

reviews.rationale: The claim holds for coding agents: a period preprint measures about 1000x over code chat. It fails for agentic workflows in general: Gartner's period estimate is 5-30x, below the 100x the plain reading requires. Since the speaker named no agent type or baseline, the evidence splits, so the outcome is mixed.
